title: Heterogeneous co-circulation of multiple DENV-1 and DENV-2 genotypes in Vung Tau during the 2023 dengue outbreak in Vietnam

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the genetic diversity and co-circulation of DENV-1 and DENV-2 genotypes during the 2023 dengue outbreak in Vung Tau, Vietnam, given the significant global health threat posed by dengue virus, particularly in hyper-endemic regions like Vietnam.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterized the 2023 dengue outbreak in Vung Tau, Vietnam, by collecting isolates from 148 hospitalized patients (66.89% adults) and performing whole-genome sequencing on 53 of these isolates.
analysis.methods: Isolates were propagated using a low-passage, antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE)-based system, and whole-genome sequencing was conducted to yield 47 consensus sequences, including 26 complete genomes.
analysis.main_results: Phylogenetic analysis revealed the co-circulation of diverse DENV-1 and DENV-2 genotypes. DENV-1 isolates were predominantly genotype I (86%) and genotype IV (14%), while DENV-2 isolates were predominantly the Cosmopolitan genotype (98%). Both genotypes showed clustering with previously reported Vietnamese and regional Southeast Asian strains, indicating ongoing local circulation and regional viral exchange.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the persistence of established DENV lineages alongside ongoing genetic diversification, providing insight into the genetic diversity and co-circulation of DENV-1 and DENV-2 during the 2023 outbreak in Vietnam.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can support future epidemiological surveillance, vaccine evaluation, and outbreak preparedness by monitoring dengue virus genetic diversity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the sample size and the fact that only 53 out of 148 isolates were sequenced, which may affect the comprehensiveness of the genetic diversity analysis. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized the 2023 dengue outbreak in Vung Tau, Vietnam, revealing the co-circulation of diverse DENV-1 and DENV-2 genotypes, with implications for future surveillance and preparedness.

title: An overview of current technologies in the development of drugs and vaccines against dengue virus.

analysis.scope_and_question: Dengue viruses 1–4 and dengue disease; other flaviviruses are near-neighbour exclusions. Biologically related animal, taxonomic, model, differential-diagnosis and comparative entities are supplementary-only unless material target-specific evidence is also present; only explicit lexical or unrelated hard exclusions are terminal.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review focuses on current technologies in the development of drugs and vaccines against dengue virus. It includes a range of studies and research efforts, with an emphasis on experimental and preclinical approaches. The review does not explicitly report on the databases used, search dates, or eligibility criteria for the studies included.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Dengue fever is a major public health hazard in tropical and subtropical areas. Current research aims to elucidate the complex host immune responses that underlie dengue pathogenesis and vaccine-induced protection, to develop more effective treatments and preventive measures. Most approaches remain at the experimental or preclinical stage and require further clinical evaluation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The WHO has approved or prequalified two live-attenuated vaccines: TAK-003 (Qdenga®) and Dengvaxia® (CYD-TDV). However, both vaccines have drawbacks, including limited effectiveness across serotypes and safety issues in seronegative individuals. Advances in treatment and prevention have mainly focused on developing vaccines and antiviral medications. While some antiviral candidates are in clinical trials, most remain in preclinical or early research stages.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Currently, no treatment for dengue fever works for everyone.

analysis.summary_en: This review provides an overview of current technologies in the development of drugs and vaccines against dengue virus. Dengue virus, with four serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4), is a major public health hazard in tropical and subtropical regions. The review highlights that while some antiviral candidates are in clinical trials, most remain in preclinical or early research stages. Two vaccines, TAK-003 (Qdenga®) and Dengvaxia® (CYD-TDV), have been approved by the WHO, but they face challenges such as limited effectiveness across serotypes and safety concerns in seronegative individuals. The review emphasizes the need for further research to better understand host immune responses and develop more effective treatments and preventive measures. Overall, the review underscores the importance of continued clinical evaluation and innovation in addressing dengue disease.

title: Characterization of acute dengue immune status and serotype surveillance in three regions of Burkina Faso: a hospital-based cross-sectional study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: In recent years, dengue has become a significant public health concern in Burkina Faso, associated with severe disease and death. Rapid characterization of acute dengue serostatus is useful for identifying patients at risk, informing transmission dynamics, and supporting public health decision-making.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multicenter study was conducted between 2023 and 2025 in Bobo-Dioulasso, Houndé, Ouagadougou, and Gaoua. Blood samples were collected from patients with suspected dengue. Acute DENV infections and serotypes were identified using real-time RT-PCR, and immune status was characterized by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) according to WHO criteria.
analysis.methods: The study aimed to characterize dengue immune status in three regions of Burkina Faso to inform pre-vaccination screening, evaluate a commercial combined DENV NS1, IgM, and IgG rapid diagnostic test (RDT) kit, and investigate DENV serotype circulation. Serum samples were screened using the reference standard (RT-PCR combined with ELISA) to evaluate the performance of a commercial DENV NS1, IgM, and IgG RDT kit in characterizing dengue immune status.
analysis.main_results: Primary dengue accounted for 75.9%, 80.4%, and 71.4% in 2023, 2024, and 2025, respectively. The sensitivity of the RDT for determining primary and post-primary dengue during the first 5 days of illness was 93.3% and 94.7%, respectively. DENV-1, DENV-2, and DENV-3 accounted for 47.0%, 5.6%, and 47.4% of cases, respectively. DENV-4 was not detected. The diagnostic specificity of the RDT for both primary and post-primary dengue was 100%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Primary dengue cases predominated, while severe dengue was associated with post-primary infection. The RDT proved to be a useful point-of-care tool for discriminating dengue immune status.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may help inform future vaccination strategies. The study provides insights into the serotype circulation and immune status of dengue cases, which can support public health decision-making.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in three regions of Burkina Faso, which may limit generalisability. The evidence is strong, with high sensitivity and specificity of the RDT for determining dengue immune status.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterizes dengue immune status and serotype circulation in three regions of Burkina Faso using a hospital-based cross-sectional design. It evaluates the performance of a commercial DENV NS1, IgM, and IgG RDT kit and identifies primary and post-primary dengue cases. The results show that primary dengue cases predominated, with DENV-1 and DENV-3 being the most common serotypes. The RDT demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for detecting dengue immune status. These findings may inform future vaccination strategies and public health decision-making, although the study's regional focus may limit generalisability.

title: Regional and Temporal Dynamics of Dengue in Mexico (2020-2024): A Comprehensive Epidemiological Analysis.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the regional and temporal dynamics of dengue in Mexico from 2020 to 2024, examining geographic distribution, temporal trends, serotype dynamics, and disease severity. The central question is to understand how dengue transmission patterns have evolved over this period and their implications for public health.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review utilizes national surveillance data from 2020 to 2024 to provide a comprehensive overview of dengue's changing epidemiological landscape. The study design includes analysis of serotype-specific data, climatic factors, and hospitalization rates. The review does not explicitly mention meta-analysis or consensus processes, but it relies on systematic data collection and interpretation.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review reports a fivefold increase in dengue cases in Mexico from 2020 to 2024, with DENV3 becoming dominant by 2024. It also highlights a shift in predominant serotypes over the years, with DENV2, DENV1, and DENV3 showing varying prevalence. Additionally, it notes that severe dengue remained below 5% of cases, while warning signs increased significantly.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies a shift in seasonal patterns, with transmission extending into unusual winter months from late 2023. It also notes that while DENV3 dominated nationally, DENV1 and DENV2 persisted in specific states, and DENV4 circulated sporadically. These findings suggest heterogeneity in transmission dynamics, which may be influenced by climatic factors and regional differences.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for regional surveillance, prevention, and clinical preparedness strategies due to the heterogeneous and dynamic nature of dengue transmission in Mexico. It also highlights the importance of monitoring serotype-specific trends and their impact on disease severity and hospitalization rates.

analysis.summary_en: This review provides a comprehensive analysis of dengue dynamics in Mexico from 2020 to 2024, focusing on geographic distribution, temporal trends, serotype shifts, and disease severity. It reports a fivefold increase in dengue cases, with DENV3 becoming dominant by 2024. The study highlights the shift in predominant serotypes over the years and notes that severe dengue remained below 5% of cases. Seasonal patterns have changed, with transmission extending into winter months. The findings underscore the need for regional surveillance and tailored prevention strategies. The review also identifies gaps in understanding serotype-specific severity and the role of climatic factors in transmission dynamics.

title: Solanaceae-Derived Spirostane Saponins Inhibit Dengue Virus Replication and Viral Protein Expression and Exhibit Activity Against Multiple Arboviruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the unmet need for specific antiviral therapies against mosquito-borne arboviruses, particularly dengue virus (DENV), by identifying novel antiviral compounds from plant-derived natural products.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a bioactivity-guided approach to screen methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species for antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells.
analysis.methods: Methanolic extracts from Solanaceae species were screened for antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Functional assays were used to evaluate viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Structural characterization was performed using UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Molecular docking analyses were conducted to predict interactions with key viral enzymes.
analysis.main_results: Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Functional assays demonstrated that the isolated spirostane-type steroidal saponins inhibited DENV replication, with marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. These compounds also retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that spirostane saponins are promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings could inform the development of new antiviral therapies for dengue and other related arboviruses, potentially reducing the global health burden of these infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of a single DENV-2 strain and the absence of in vivo studies, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the in vitro nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study identified spirostane saponins from Solanaceae plants as promising antiviral compounds against DENV-2 and other related arboviruses, supporting their further development for broad-spectrum antiviral therapies.

title: Computational Insights Into the Conformational Dynamics of the Dengue Virus Capsid Protein.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the conformational dynamics of the Dengue virus capsid protein, focusing on the hydrophobic pocket's role in viral lifecycle functions and transitions between open and closed conformations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research employed molecular dynamics simulations and enhanced sampling methods to study the conformational change pathway of the capsid protein.
analysis.methods: Molecular dynamics simulations and enhanced sampling methods were used to investigate the structural rearrangements governing the transitions of the capsid protein's hydrophobic pocket.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that lipid binding modulates the accessibility of the hydrophobic pocket, and the open conformation facilitates interactions with lipids and virus assembly, while the closed conformation protects the pocket from aqueous media and premature interactions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as providing insights into the capsid protein's conformational dynamics, which could be targeted for antiviral strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These insights could inform the development of antiviral strategies targeting the capsid protein's functional transitions, potentially impacting the prevention and treatment of dengue virus infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the reliance on computational methods, which may not fully capture all aspects of the capsid protein's behavior in vivo.

analysis.summary_en: This study used molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the conformational dynamics of the Dengue virus capsid protein, revealing that lipid binding modulates the hydrophobic pocket's accessibility and that the open conformation facilitates virus assembly, while the closed conformation protects the pocket from aqueous media. These insights could inform antiviral strategies targeting the capsid protein's functional transitions.

title: Targeting CLK1 by CRISPR tools and pharmacological inhibition modulates the innate immune response and dengue virus replication

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate splicing changes shared between dengue virus (DENV) infection and interferon (IFN) treatment in cultured cells, as these alterations are known to arise from both direct viral interference and cellular responses such as activation of innate immunity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in cultured cells, using interferon treatment as a model for virus-independent innate immune activation, and focused on dengue virus infection and IFN treatment.
analysis.methods: The researchers used CRISPR/dCas9-mediated modulation of CLK1 expression in stable cell lines and pharmacological inhibition of CLK1 kinase activity with TG003 to assess its impact on immune response gene induction and DENV replication.
analysis.main_results: The study found that silencing CLK1 enhanced the induction of immune response genes, while its over-expression attenuated it. Additionally, inhibition of CLK1 kinase activity with TG003 further potentiated IFN-induced gene expression and reduced DENV replication.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that CLK1 acts as a proviral negative regulator of IFN-stimulated gene expression, and its inhibition could enhance antiviral defenses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into potential therapeutic strategies targeting CLK1 to enhance antiviral defenses against dengue virus.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to cultured cells and does not account for in vivo conditions, but the evidence is strong as it directly links CLK1 modulation to changes in immune response and DENV replication.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates splicing changes shared between dengue virus (DENV) infection and interferon (IFN) treatment in cultured cells. It identifies CLK1 as a gene whose expression is altered during these processes, with increased non-coding mRNA isoforms observed. The researchers used CRISPR/dCas9 and pharmacological inhibitors to modulate CLK1 expression and found that silencing CLK1 enhanced immune response gene induction, while its over-expression reduced it. Inhibition of CLK1 kinase activity with TG003 further potentiated IFN-induced gene expression and reduced DENV replication. These results suggest CLK1 as a proviral negative regulator of IFN-stimulated gene expression, indicating its potential as a therapeutic target. The study's findings are significant for understanding antiviral defenses but are limited to in vitro models.

title: Impact of temperature on patient-derived dengue virus breakthrough infections in wMel-infected Aedes aegypti

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study investigates how temperature affects the protection provided by the w Mel strain of Wolbachia against dengue virus (DENV) transmission in Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, building on prior evidence that Wolbachia reduces dengue incidence.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a laboratory model with viremic blood collected from 13 dengue inpatients at the Hospital for Tropical Diseases in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, to assess temperature effects on w Mel-infected Ae.
analysis.methods: The researchers reared w Mel-infected Ae. aegypti mosquitoes at two temperatures (28 ± 4°C and 31 ± 4°C) and assessed the development of infectious saliva following a viremic blood meal, as well as the density of Wolbachia in key tissues and DENV replication levels.
analysis.main_results: Mosquitoes reared at 31 ± 4°C developed infectious saliva more frequently than those at 28 ± 4°C, but the risk was still lower than in w Mel-free mosquitoes. Heat treatment reduced Wolbachia density in tissues and increased DENV replication in the head/thorax, with higher DENV RNA levels associated with increased odds of infectious saliva development.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that elevated temperatures may increase the risk of DENV breakthrough infections in w Mel-infected mosquitoes, potentially due to increased DENV replication in these mosquitoes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results highlight the need for increased surveillance in high-temperature regions or during heat waves to monitor changes in Wolbachia frequency and DENV infection rates in Ae. aegypti populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a laboratory setting, and the observed effects may not fully reflect real-world conditions. However, the evidence is strong as it directly links temperature changes to Wolbachia density and DENV replication in mosquitoes.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines how temperature influences the protective effect of the w Mel Wolbachia strain against dengue virus (DENV) in Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. Using viremic blood from dengue patients, the researchers found that higher rearing temperatures (31°C) increased the risk of DENV breakthrough infections in w Mel-infected mosquitoes compared to those at 28°C. Despite this, the risk remained lower than in w Mel-free mosquitoes. The study highlights the importance of temperature in modulating Wolbachia's ability to suppress DENV replication, suggesting that surveillance should be intensified in high-temperature environments to monitor potential changes in DENV transmission dynamics. The findings are based on laboratory experiments and provide specific insights into the interplay between temperature, Wolbachia density, and DENV replication in mosquitoes, with moderate confidence due to the controlled setting.

title: Peer Review Report For: Clinical Characteristics, Associated Factors, Treatment Practices, and Outcomes of Dengue Fever among Adult Acute Febrile Illness Cases in Las’anod, Sool Region, Somalia: A Hospital-Based Cross-Sectional Study [version 1; peer review: 1 approved with reservations]

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics, associated factors, treatment practices, and outcomes of dengue fever among adult acute febrile illness cases in Las’anod, Sool Region, Somalia. The background highlights the importance of understanding fever as a host defense mechanism against infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a hospital-based cross-sectional study conducted in Las’anod, Sool Region, Somalia, focusing on adult patients with acute febrile illness. The study included cases of dengue fever and compared them with other febrile illnesses.
analysis.methods: The study involved collecting data on clinical characteristics, associated factors, treatment practices, and outcomes from adult patients with acute febrile illness. It used a cross-sectional design to analyze the data and assess the role of fever in the context of dengue infection.
analysis.main_results: Randomized clinical trials that lowered body temperature showed either no benefit, increased morbidity, or a trend toward increased mortality. These findings suggest that reducing fever may not be beneficial in self-limited infections like dengue fever.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these results as supporting the idea that fever is a protective response to infection, consistent with the broader body of research on its role as a host defense mechanism. This study adds to the evidence that fever may be beneficial in dengue infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have implications for the management of dengue fever, suggesting that antipyretic drugs may not be recommended for reducing fever in self-limited infections. They also highlight the need for further research on the role of fever in dengue disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which does not establish causality. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on observational studies and randomized trials, but it is consistent with the broader understanding of fever as a protective response.

analysis.summary_en: This hospital-based cross-sectional study in Las’anod, Sool Region, Somalia, examined the clinical characteristics, associated factors, treatment practices, and outcomes of dengue fever among adult acute febrile illness cases. The study found that randomized clinical trials lowering body temperature showed no benefit or increased morbidity in self-limited infections. These results align with the broader scientific consensus that fever is a protective host defense mechanism against infections. The findings suggest that antipyretic drugs may not be beneficial for reducing fever in dengue infections and highlight the need for further research. The study's cross-sectional design limits its ability to establish causality, and the evidence is considered moderate due to reliance on observational data and trials. The results contribute to the understanding of fever's role in dengue disease and have implications for clinical management and future research.

title: COST RECOVERY RATE OF HOSPITAL TARIFFS AND INA-CBGs REIMBURSEMENT FOR DENGUE HAEMORRHAGIC FEVER (DHF) AT TYPE C HOSPITAL IN INDONESIA

analysis.scope_and_question: This study aimed to analyze the Cost Recovery Rate (CRR) by comparing hospital tariffs, INA-CBGs reimbursement, and the actual cost of treating Grade I Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever (DHF) patients while identifying factors contributing to cost discrepancies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A qualitative single embedded case study was conducted at a Type C private hospital in Palembang, Indonesia. Secondary financial and clinical data from 35 Class III inpatients with Grade I DHF were analyzed alongside semi-structured interviews with five key informants representing hospital management, clinical services, finance, and the casemix unit. Data were analyzed through document review, cost comparison, CRR calculation, and thematic analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The findings revealed differences between the hospital's internal tariff (Rp82,925,300), INA-CBGs reimbursement (Rp69,730,500), and the actual treatment cost (Rp72,479,198). The resulting Cost Recovery Rate (CRR) of 96.21% indicated that INA-CBGs reimbursement was insufficient to fully recover the actual cost of care.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The financing gap was influenced by the interaction of several factors, including the package-based INA-CBGs payment mechanism, length of hospital stay, patients' clinical conditions, diagnosis and procedure coding accuracy, adherence to clinical pathways, laboratory and pharmaceutical utilization, and overall hospital resource efficiency.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Strengthening clinical pathway adherence, documentation and coding accuracy, resource utilization, and cost monitoring may improve hospital financial performance while maintaining the quality and safety of patient care.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the cost recovery rate (CRR) of hospital tariffs and INA-CBGs reimbursement for treating Grade I Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever (DHF) patients at a Type C private hospital in Indonesia. The research highlights discrepancies between the hospital's internal tariff, INA-CBGs reimbursement, and actual treatment costs, revealing a CRR of 96.21%. This suggests that the current reimbursement system does not fully cover the cost of care. The study identifies several factors contributing to these financial gaps, including the package-based payment mechanism, length of hospital stay, clinical conditions, coding accuracy, adherence to clinical pathways, and resource efficiency. The findings emphasize the need for integrated clinical and operational management to enhance financial sustainability. Recommendations include improving clinical pathway adherence, documentation accuracy, resource utilization, and cost monitoring to support better hospital financial performance without compromising patient care quality.

title: A High-Content Pseudotime Framework for Morphological Profiling of Dengue Virus Inhibitors from a Drug-Repurposing Library

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify DENV antivirals due to the global prevalence of dengue fever and the lack of FDA-approved antivirals, as well as the risk of severe dengue fever from the available vaccine.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized a drug repurposing approach with high-content screening and machine learning to screen 960 compounds for antiviral efficacy against DENV.
analysis.methods: High-content screening was performed in a DENV infection model to characterize morphological patterns of NS4B and envelope (E) protein expression over time, and a viral pseudotime model was developed to predict infection progression. A single cell infection classifier was used for antiviral efficacy, and a pseudotime machine learning model was trained to score concentration-dependent inhibitors.
analysis.main_results: Four concentration-dependent inhibitors of DENV were identified: esomeprazole, GW4064, pralatrexate, and LY411575, with potencies ranging from nanomolar to submicromolar.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: LY411575, a gamma secretase inhibitor, exhibited an IC50 of 72 nM and reduced percent infection to near the level of the mock infection control, indicating its potential as a DENV antiviral.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting early stages of the viral life cycle with inhibitors like LY411575 could be a promising strategy for preventing severe dengue fever.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the need for further validation of the identified inhibitors in clinical settings and the potential for off-target effects.

analysis.summary_en: This study identified four DENV antivirals, with LY411575 showing promising efficacy in reducing infection levels. The findings suggest targeting early viral stages could prevent severe dengue fever.

title: Genomic Diversity, Phylogenetic Structure, and In Silico Diagnostic Primer Compatibility of Available DENV-1 Genotype V from Mexico

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue virus serotype 1 (DENV-1) is prevalent across the Americas, yet its genomic diversity in Mexico is poorly characterized.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We analyzed 119 public Mexican DENV-1 genomes (polyprotein CDS, 10,179 nt) alongside 111 from 19 other American countries and territories.
analysis.methods: The Mexican panel was temporally and geographically uneven (91% from 2006 to 2009), representing available sequences, not nationwide diversity.
analysis.main_results: The Mexican genotype V sequences formed 115 haplotypes (Hd = 0.9994; π = 0.00831), resolving into clades A (n = 6) and B (n = 112) plus one independent introduction in Jalisco.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These sequences were not monophyletic: both clades grouped with Nicaraguan and United States viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Their common ancestor dated to 1977.5 and clade divergence to 1984.2.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Selection appeared to be predominantly purifying (ω = 0.037); no site showed concordant evidence of diversifying selection, and no recombination was detected.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the genomic diversity of DENV-1 genotype V in Mexico, revealing substantial haplotype diversity and multiple introductions. The Mexican sequences formed 115 haplotypes, resolving into clades A and B, with one independent introduction in Jalisco. These sequences were not monophyletic, grouping with Nicaraguan and United States viruses. The common ancestor of these sequences dated to 1977.5, and clade divergence occurred around 1984.2. The study found predominantly purifying selection and no evidence of diversifying selection or recombination. In silico diagnostic primer compatibility showed 84% of Mexican sequences matched all three CDC real-time oligonucleotides. The findings highlight the need for periodic in silico primer revalidation to ensure accurate detection of DENV-1 genotype V in Mexico.

title: A single dose of Dengvaxia is associated with transient reduction in dengue infection risk among dengue-naïve children

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the impact of a single dose of Dengvaxia on the susceptibility to wild-type (WT) dengue virus (DENV) infection among dengue-naïve children, addressing the uncertainty regarding the durability of vaccine-induced immunity and its effect on subsequent infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A longitudinal cohort study of 186 seronegative children, including 114 who received a single dose of Dengvaxia and 72 who remained unvaccinated, was conducted over 40 months.
analysis.methods: Samples were collected at baseline and two follow-up time points (20 months [T1] and 40 months [T2]) and analyzed using yellow fever virus (YFV) non-structural protein 1 (NS1) antibody assays to differentiate between vaccine-associated and WT infection-induced responses.
analysis.main_results: At T1, 61% of vaccinated children were responders. During the first follow-up period (baseline-T1), vaccination was associated with a reduced risk of WT DENV infection (vaccine effectiveness [VE]=45%). Low-level YFV NS1 responses remained detectable through T2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that a single dose of Dengvaxia in dengue-naïve children was associated with a reduced risk of WT DENV infection and with differences in subsequent antibody responses during the first follow-up period, but these associations were no longer observed during the second period.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results have implications for understanding the long-term efficacy of Dengvaxia and the immune response following WT DENV infection, which could inform future vaccine strategies and surveillance efforts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations include the potential for confounding factors and the need for a larger sample size to generalize findings. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the impact of a single dose of Dengvaxia on susceptibility to wild-type dengue virus infection among dengue-naïve children, finding a reduced risk of infection during the first follow-up period but no difference during the second period.

title: Unilateral Vocal Cord Paresis in Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever: A Rare Delayed Immune-mediated Neurological Manifestation and Complete Recovery

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to document a rare neurological complication of dengue hemorrhagic fever, specifically unilateral vocal cord paresis, and to highlight its potential as a delayed immune-mediated manifestation. Dengue virus is a significant public health threat, particularly in endemic regions, with evolving clinical presentations that require further understanding.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a case report describing an 18-year-old female patient with dengue hemorrhagic fever who developed unilateral vocal cord paresis on day 14 of fever. The patient was admitted to the ICU with dengue shock syndrome and traumatic liver injury, and her clinical course included significant initial abnormalities such as hemoglobin drop, thrombocytopenia, and elevated transaminases.
analysis.methods: The patient was diagnosed with dengue based on NS1 antigen positivity on day 1. Her clinical presentation, including neurological symptoms, was documented through medical records and physical examination. Laboratory tests were conducted to assess blood parameters, liver function, and other metabolic indicators.
analysis.main_results: The patient developed left vocal cord palsy on day 14 of fever, which resolved spontaneously without intervention. She was admitted to the ICU with dengue shock syndrome and traumatic liver injury, and her initial abnormalities included a hemoglobin drop (7.4 gm/dL), thrombocytopenia, elevated transaminases, and reduced albumin.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret this case as an example of a rare, delayed immune-mediated peripheral nervous system complication in dengue patients. This finding adds to the growing recognition of diverse neurological manifestations associated with dengue infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This case highlights the importance of considering immune-mediated neurological complications in dengue patients, particularly those with severe dengue. It underscores the need for vigilance in monitoring neurological symptoms in dengue-infected individuals.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: As a case report, the study provides limited generalizability and lacks statistical analysis. However, the evidence is strong for the specific case described, offering a unique insight into dengue's potential neurological complications.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes an 18-year-old female with dengue hemorrhagic fever who developed unilateral vocal cord paresis on day 14 of fever, followed by spontaneous recovery. The patient was admitted to the ICU with dengue shock syndrome and traumatic liver injury, presenting with significant initial abnormalities such as hemoglobin drop, thrombocytopenia, and elevated transaminases. The study highlights a rare, delayed immune-mediated neurological complication of dengue, contributing to the understanding of its diverse clinical manifestations. While the study is limited by its case report design, the findings provide valuable insight into the potential neurological effects of dengue infection, emphasizing the need for vigilance in monitoring patients for such complications.

title: Entomological response to control interventions during the first chikungunya and dengue outbreak in White Nile, Sudan.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The present study evaluates the entomological response following an integrated vector management package implemented during the outbreak in Tandalti town.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Stegomyia indices together with per-container productivity of larvae and pupae were calculated to quantify container infestation and evaluate entomological changes following the intervention.
analysis.methods: Longitudinal entomological surveillance across 10 clusters encompassing 600 households and 2500 containers was conducted from July to December 2022.
analysis.main_results: Following the implementation of control interventions, Stegomyia indices decreased substantially from September to December (house index by 78.2%, container index by 35.1%, Breteau index by 92.8% and pupal/demographic index by 94.1%) and total immatures decreased by 89.5% (larvae) and 95.5% (pupae).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The decrease in vector density is a combined effect of the control interventions and the wet to dry seasonal transition.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Sustained post-outbreak surveillance is needed, as these residual containers may contribute to vector population resurgence during subsequent transmission seasons.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Combining Stegomyia indices with per-container productivity identifies and quantifies residual containers sustaining the vector population.

analysis.summary_en: The present study evaluates the entomological response following an integrated vector management package implemented during the outbreak in Tandalti town. Stegomyia indices together with per-container productivity of larvae and pupae were calculated to quantify container infestation and evaluate entomological changes following the intervention. Longitudinal entomological surveillance across 10 clusters encompassing 600 households and 2500 containers was conducted from July to December 2022. Following the implementation of control interventions, Stegomyia indices decreased substantially from September to December (house index by 78.2%, container index by 35.1%, Breteau index by 92.8% and pupal/demographic index by 94.1%) and total immatures decreased by 89.5% (larvae) and 95.5% (pupae). The decrease in vector density is a combined effect of the control interventions and the wet to dry seasonal transition. Sustained post-outbreak surveillance is needed, as these residual containers may contribute to vector population resurgence during subsequent transmission seasons. Combining Stegomyia indices with per-container productivity identifies and quantifies residual containers sustaining the vector population.

title: DENGUE, ZIKA, AND CHIKUNGUNYA AMONG INDIGENOUS POPULATIONS IN AMAZONAS: EPIDEMIOLOGICAL ANALYSIS FROM 2021 TO 2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: The spread of arboviruses into Indigenous territories highlights a critical socio‐environmental vulnerability and epidemiological transition, creating a need to document disease occurrence in this population; the study aimed to describe cases of Dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika among Indigenous people in Amazonas.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a retrospective descriptive analysis of 2021‐2025 surveillance data, and Indigenous individuals represented 868 cases (2.65%) of the 32,730 total notifications.
analysis.methods: A retrospective descriptive study analyzed surveillance bulletin data from 2021 to 2025, without experimental intervention, to characterize arbovirus cases.
analysis.main_results: Between January 2021 and December 2025, 32,730 arbovirus cases were reported in Amazonas, comprising 95.94% Dengue, 2.02% Zika, and 2.04% Chikungunya. Female cases represented about 52% of all infections, and 868 (2.65%) of cases occurred among Indigenous individuals, with higher proportions in the 20‐29 age group, while infants under one year and persons aged 60+ had specific percentages for each virus. The highest case counts were observed in the municipalities of Manaus, Tabatinga, and São Paulo de Olivença.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that preventing uncontrolled arboviral emergence in Indigenous Amazonas requires health surveillance, cultural respect, and territorial protection beyond the traditional urban model.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform targeted surveillance, culturally appropriate prevention, and territorial protection strategies for Indigenous communities to mitigate arboviral risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The retrospective descriptive design based on surveillance bulletin data may suffer underreporting and limited demographic detail, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: The study provides an epidemiological overview of Dengue, Zika, and Chikungunya infections among Indigenous peoples in Amazonas from 2021 to 2025. A retrospective descriptive analysis of surveillance bulletin data captured 32,730 total arbovirus cases, of which 95.94% were Dengue, 2.02% Zika, and 2.04% Chikungunya. Female cases accounted for roughly 52% of infections, and 868 individuals (2.65%) were Indigenous, with the highest proportion in the 20‐29 age group; specific age‐group percentages were also identified for infants and the elderly. The highest case counts occurred in Manaus, Tabatinga, and São Paulo de Olivença. The authors emphasize that effective prevention must move beyond urban models, incorporating culturally sensitive surveillance, respect for local traditions, and territorial protection to curb uncontrolled arboviral emergence in this vulnerable population.

title: Phytochemical profiling, characterization, and antiviral evaluation of hydro alcoholic bark extract of Alstonia scholaris (L.) against DENV-2

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the antiviral activity of hydroalcoholic bark extract of Alstonia scholaris against DENV-2, addressing the lack of effective antiviral drugs for dengue disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study designed and extracted hydroalcoholic bark extract of Alstonia scholaris and evaluated its antiviral activity against DENV-2 using Vero CCL-81 cells.
analysis.methods: The hydroalcoholic extract was prepared using a Soxhlet apparatus, and phytochemical analysis confirmed the presence of alkaloids, glycosides, flavonoids, and steroids. UV-Visible spectroscopy and FTIR analysis were used to identify functional groups, and HPTLC profiling quantified stigmasterol content. Cytotoxicity and antiviral studies were conducted using the MTT assay and pre, co, and post-treatment conditions.
analysis.main_results: The hydroalcoholic bark extract demonstrated moderate inhibitory activity against DENV-2 during pre, co, and post-treatment conditions. The CC50 value was 105.5 μg/mL at 120 h, indicating time-dependent cytotoxicity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the hydroalcoholic bark extract of Alstonia scholaris possesses potential antiviral activity against DENV-2, making it a promising natural source for further pharmacological exploration.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results could inform future studies on natural antiviral compounds and contribute to the development of new treatments for dengue disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of a single cell line and the need for further validation. The evidence strength is moderate due to the abstract-only nature of the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the antiviral activity of hydroalcoholic bark extract of Alstonia scholaris against DENV-2, demonstrating moderate inhibitory activity. The findings suggest potential for further pharmacological exploration and contribute to the development of new treatments for dengue disease.

title: Zika virus produces two isoforms of the NS2A protein that play mutually exclusive roles in viral replication and virion assembly.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Zika virus (ZIKV), dengue virus, and several other orthoflaviviruses cause disease outbreaks in human and animal populations worldwide. The orthoflaviviral nonstructural protein 2A (NS2A) is critical for both viral replication and virion assembly.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using endogenously tagged NS2A-containing viral RNAs to investigate the presence and roles of NS2A isoforms during ZIKV infection.
analysis.methods: Phylogenetic and conservation analyses combined with polyprotein cleavage assays were used to determine the generation and conservation of both NS2A isoforms across the Orthoflavivirus genus.
analysis.main_results: The study revealed that two NS2A isoforms are present during ZIKV infection, including both full-length NS2A and a C-terminally truncated isoform, termed NS2Aα.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that both NS2A isoforms are generated via the viral protease and are conserved across the Orthoflavivirus genus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides insights into the form and function of the NS2A protein, which could inform future research on viral replication and virion assembly mechanisms in orthoflaviviruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the findings are based on in vitro assays, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the roles of two NS2A isoforms in Zika virus infection, revealing their distinct functions in viral replication and virion assembly. The research highlights the importance of NS2A in the orthoflaviviral life cycle and suggests that these isoforms play mutually exclusive roles. The findings contribute to understanding the molecular mechanisms of ZIKV and may inform future studies on viral protein function. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence and in vitro assays, which may limit its generalizability to real-world conditions.

title: Frequentist and Bayesian Interval Estimation for Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Incidence Rates with Application to Dengue Fever Surveillance

analysis.research_question_and_background: A reliable interval estimation of the latent mean incidence rate is important but challenging in infectious disease surveillance because count data are often zero-inflated and overdispersed.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study compared frequentist (normal approximation (NA), bootstrap percentile (BP), and bootstrap-t (BT)) and Bayesian (equal-tailed interval (ETI) and highest density interval (HDI)) intervals under the zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model.
analysis.methods: A Monte Carlo simulation study varied levels of zero inflation, dispersion, and the observation period, evaluating conditional and unconditional coverage and average interval length.
analysis.main_results: NA and BP showed undercoverage throughout the evaluated scenarios.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: BT improved conditional coverage over BP in 47 of 54 scenarios but generally produced wider intervals.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Bayesian intervals often had higher coverage, although overcoverage and diagnostic failures prevented a uniform advantage.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: HDI was shorter than ETI in every scenario.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to improve interval estimation for zero-inflated and overdispersed incidence rates in dengue fever surveillance. It compared frequentist and Bayesian methods under a zero-inflated negative binomial model, using Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate coverage and interval length. The results showed that frequentist methods like NA and BP had undercoverage, while BT improved conditional coverage in most scenarios but resulted in wider intervals. Bayesian intervals generally had higher coverage, though overcoverage and diagnostic failures limited their uniform advantage. HDI was consistently shorter than ETI. The study highlights the importance of selecting appropriate interval estimation methods for dengue surveillance data, emphasizing that no single method uniformly achieves nominal coverage. These findings can inform more accurate surveillance practices and highlight the need for careful method selection based on data characteristics.
